stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: a returning client resumed with its ticket, its 0-RTT GET reached the app with Early-Data: 1 before the handshake finished, and a replayed copy of that first flight ran the GET again.
stamps.test: TLS > resumption, 0-RTT and a replayed first flight (resumption)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: http:// got a 301 to https://, every HTTPS answer (even a 404) carried the header, and curl, having seen it once, went straight to https:// the next time.
stamps.test: TLS > HSTS: redirect once, then https:// before anything is sent (downgrade-hsts)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: with a leaf + intermediate chain like this one, OpenSSL 4.0.2 printed every line shown here.
stamps.test: TLS > what openssl s_client prints: the chain, and Mallory's fakes (chain-of-trust, fake-certificates)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: serving each of Mallory's certificates in turn, OpenSSL 4.0.2 stopped with exactly these errors.
stamps.test: TLS > what openssl s_client prints: the chain, and Mallory's fakes (chain-of-trust, fake-certificates)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: curl got HTTP/2 through ALPN with the Alt-Svc header, and nginx opened the UDP port for QUIC. HTTP/3 itself wasn't tested: there's no HTTP/3 client here.
stamps.test: HTTP versions > HTTP/2 through ALPN, the Alt-Svc header, and a UDP port for QUIC (alt-svc)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: the upgrade got 101 and messages flowed both ways. With the Upgrade and Connection lines removed, the chat server got a plain GET and the handshake failed.
stamps.test: WebSockets > the upgrade through nginx: 101, then messages both ways (one-server-per-socket)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: removing any one of the five servers moved about a fifth of the URIs. With plain hash $uri, about four in five moved.
stamps.test: Consistent hashing > hash $uri consistent moves about 1/N; without it, about 4 in 5 (a-server-leaves)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: one master process plus one worker per core, each worker with a single thread.
stamps.test: Processes and threads > a master and one single-threaded worker per core (databases-and-web-servers)

stamps.note: Ran it on nginx 1.31.6: /cart came back with no-store and the hashed CSS with the one-year immutable header, over a connection that was still open after a minute of silence.
stamps.test: idle connections > a minute of silence: keep-alive, proxy_read_timeout and heartbeats (why-its-faster, one-server-per-socket, heartbeats)
